reading.body:
Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County has published neither its power consumption nor its building footprint, placing it outside the four Tennessee data center campuses with disclosed megawatt figures. The site remains ranked fifth among mapped facilities in the state by some measure, though that ranking cannot be derived from published capacity. Meta states it has invested $1.5 billion and broke ground in 2020, suggesting a mature operational phase, but the actual IT load serving AI workloads is not disclosed.

The campus operates under a commitment to match 100 percent of electricity use with renewable energy and aims to be water positive by 2030. Meta reports that a supported project is adding 530 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity in Tennessee. Without a published power figure for the campus itself, this state-level renewable deployment cannot be directly attributed to powering Gallatin, and the grid constraint on this site's growth remains unknown.

Operational buildings hold LEED Gold certification, confirming environmental controls typical of modern hyperscale facilities. Meta employs 70 or more staff once full build-out completes and reports direct local investment in schools and nonprofits. For readers assessing whether Gallatin matters to AI scaling, the absence of published capacity data prevents any calculation of its marginal contribution to national or regional compute supply.
